profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point, tagged simply Arpac, corresponds to a real facility of ARPAC, the Agenzia Regionale per la Protezione Ambientale in Campania, or Campania Regional Environmental Protection Agency, specifically its Benevento departmental laboratories, housed in the Mediateca Spina Verde building on Via Napoli in Benevento, Italy, provided to the agency by the municipality on a free loan basis and made fully operational in late December 2021. This registry found no evidence that the site functions as a computing data center in the conventional colocation or enterprise IT sense; rather, it houses ARPACs analytical laboratories, occupying a semi-basement level of lab and technical space with upper floors used for administrative offices, front desk services, and educational or exhibition activities. The labs analytical work spans support for law enforcement on controlled substance analysis, food safety testing on behalf of the local health authority, water quality analysis of distributed drinking water and wastewater, and support for atmospheric pollutant monitoring. This Benevento site replaced ARPACs older Via San Pasquale location for laboratory functions, though that original site continues to house departmental administration and territorial services. ARPAC itself is headquartered at Via Vicinale Santa Maria del Pianto 2 to 6 in Naples, Italy, and operates as the Campania regions environmental monitoring and regulatory agency across air, water, and soil quality, running its own internal IT systems to support that mission, though this registry could not confirm this Benevento building specifically as a dedicated data center facility. Benevento is a provincial capital in inland Campania, and consolidating ARPACs analytical laboratory functions there, separate from the departmental administration retained at the older Via San Pasquale site, reflects a broader pattern of Italian regional environmental agencies splitting specialized laboratory operations from general administrative offices across multiple buildings within the same province, an organizational choice distinct from the single consolidated headquarters model used by some other public agencies tracked elsewhere in this registry.
